concepts.title: The Hand Fan Across Regions and Materials
concepts.definition: The text surveys the hand fan or pankha across India - made of bamboo, cane, palm leaf, silk, brass or leather, decorated in every regional style - showing how one humble object carries the craft identity of many communities.
concepts.key_idea: One fan, many hands: materials and decoration make each pankha a regional signature.
concepts.textbook_ref: iebe103.txt sections on pankhas of different regions and materials
question_patterns: what materials were used to make traditional hand fans
how could each kind of pankha be distinguished from another
describe the hand fan of the region you know best
why is the pankha called a craft object - explain
compare hand fans of two different regions
what do decorations on fans tell about their users

solution_steps.explain: Bamboo, cane, palm leaf, silk, brass and leather each shaped a fan style.
Different states developed their own designs and decoration.
Fans carried art, status and daily comfort together.

concepts.title: The Theme - Winds of Change
concepts.definition: The title plays on wind: the hand fan that once stirred breeze has given way to electric fans and coolers, and with that change old crafts fade - the text invites reflection on what progress takes even as it gives.
concepts.key_idea: Change has two winds: comfort arrives and heritage retires - both must be counted.
question_patterns: why is the text titled Winds of Change - explain the play on words
what replaced the hand fan in modern homes
should we preserve crafts like fan making - discuss
how does the text contrast the past and the present
what is gained and what is lost when old crafts disappear
suggest ways to keep traditional fan making alive

solution_steps.explain: Fans move wind; the essay is about breeze makers.
Winds of change also mean the modern shift away from hand fans.
Progress and heritage both deserve thoughtful handling.

concepts.title: Descriptive Writing Features
concepts.definition: The text is a piece of descriptive-expository writing: it classifies fans by material and region, uses precise vocabulary for craft details, and organises description from form to function - a model for students' own descriptive essays.
concepts.key_idea: Classify, describe, explain: the essay's structure is itself a lesson.
question_patterns: what type of text is Winds of Change - justify
how does the writer organise the description of fans
list the craft words used in the text and their meanings
which words create pictures of the fans in your mind
write a descriptive paragraph on an object from your home
how does classification make description clearer

solution_steps.explain: Material-wise and region-wise grouping keeps it clear.
Use classification and precise words in your own writing.
